english.title: Fail to comply with regulation regulating the loading and making waterborne of export goods / passengers
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed to comply with a regulation made under section 66(1) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979

(A)_[regulating the loading and making waterborn for loading of goods for exportation or as stores and the embarking of passengers for a destination outside the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man]_
(B)_[requiring delivery of a manifest containing particulars of the cargo carried in an exporting ship and documents relating to the cargo]_
(C)_[requiring delivery of a certificate of the fuel shipped in a ship departing from a port for a place outside the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man]_

in that **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE NON-COMPLIANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66(1) and (2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes:
(i) Section 66(2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979 provides that goods in respect of which the offence was committed shall be liable to forfeiture.
(ii) This section was amended by Schedule 7 to the Taxation (Cross Border Trade) Act 2020, brought into force on the 31st December 2020 by SI 2020/1642. For any offences committed on or after the 31st December 2020, see offence document H100292 (CJS code CE79380).
